transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… thanks for seeing me. I’m probably making too much of it, but I’ve been having these moments where I get hit out of nowhere with… with the scene of my cousin on the pavement. It’s like I can hear the shouting again, see the lights, even when I’m just standing in the church office trying to act normal.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been hard to shake.
Since that incident with your cousin, have you found yourself avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened, or feeling emotionally detached from others?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m trying to be dramatic about it or anything, but I do kind of… adjust my route now. I take the long way around town so I don’t have to pass the community center or that court.

And if someone starts bringing up that night, I usually just… I shut it down, or I find some reason to step out. I know that probably sounds like I’m not handling it right. I just don’t really want to go there in front of people.
Since the incident with your cousin, have you noticed yourself feeling on edge, overly alert, or constantly worried something bad might happen again, even in safe places?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try to tell myself I’m just being careful, you know? But I can’t really sit with my back to a door anymore.

Even at church events, when I’m supposed to be listening to people or just… being present, I catch myself watching hands, corners, cars slowing down outside. I’m always clocking where the nearest exit is. I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m not trying to be paranoid or anything, it’s just… my body acts like something could happen again.
